evidence.source: Wiktionary, citing Zhengzhang Shangfang (2003)
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 杯 as a phono-semantic compound, 木 semantic and 不 phonetic, and places it in the 不 phonetic series. In Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese reconstruction system it gives 杯 *plɯː and 不 *pɯ, *pɯʔ, *pɯ'. The reconstructed forms share an initial and rhyme nucleus but differ in the reconstructed lateral and vowel length; this is compatible with a phonetic-series relationship, not proof of exact identity. The entry also mentions 否 as a variant phonetic analysis with a speculative semantic association (‘block’), for which the inspected page gives no primary paleographic support.

evidence.field: 不 entry; Zhengzhang Old Chinese readings
evidence.text: The entry lists 不 as *pɯ, *pɯʔ, and *pɯ' in Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese system. Compared with the separately listed 杯 *plɯː, the forms share a labial onset and rhyme nucleus but differ in the recorded lateral and vowel length. This supports reporting the proposed sound-series relation without treating the readings as identical.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: No primary inscription image or reliably catalogued oracle-bone, bronze, or Chu-slip specimen for 杯 was successfully inspected. The first attested written graph and the chronology of its graphic variants therefore remain unresolved.

The received Shuowen evidence is indirect in the inspected source: the Taiwan MOE entry says 杯 itself is absent and reports Shuowen’s 桮 entry as 木 + 否 phonetic. No full facsimile of the relevant Shuowen leaf was opened in this research.

There are conflicting interpretations: a 木 + 不 phonetic-series analysis; a Shuowen-derived 木 + 否 analysis; and a scholar’s semantic proposal connecting 不 with a hollow tree remnant. Available evidence does not settle whether 不 is a historical phonetic, graphic component, or a shape reinterpreted after the fact.

No sound-loan account was established. Tibetan phor pa is mentioned on the Wiktionary page as a comparison attributed to Schuessler (2007), but that primary scholarly reference and the Tibetan lexeme’s independent history/pronunciation were not inspected. It cannot substantiate a borrowing direction or a name for a depicted vessel.

The Mencius quotation is an early textual attestation of the cup measure/object sense in a received text, but its manuscript dating and the earliest surviving physical witness were not established. Semantic pathways from vessel to measure/classifier, trophy, or other extensions were not chronologically demonstrated.
The character’s earliest graphic form, exact development from 桮/盃/other variants to modern 杯, and any possible scribal corruption remain insufficiently evidenced.

No inspected primary inscription or securely catalogued oracle-bone, bronze, or Chu-slip example of 杯 was found. The earliest attested graph and chronology of its variants remain unresolved; the Taiwan MOE dictionary reports its ancient-character and Han-slip compilation data unavailable.

The received Shuowen account is indirect here: the inspected Taiwan MOE dictionary says 杯 is absent and reports Shuowen’s seal-script 桮 as 木 + 否. The distinction between this account and later 不 analyses remains unsettled; there is no inspected early inscription to establish whether 不 was original, a graphic reinterpretation, or a phonetic component in the earliest graph.

A scholarly account in the supplied dossier proposes a hollowed-tree interpretation, but the searches in this invocation did not locate an inspected primary specimen that could test it. No claim of scribal corruption or a specific graphic transition can be established.

No sound-loan account was established. The Tibetan comparison phor pa on Wiktionary does not independently establish borrowing direction, an early word history, or the pronunciation/name of a depicted cup. A reconstructed pronoun or phonetic-series match cannot establish a vessel’s original name.

The MOE entry quotes Mencius, Gaozi I, for 一杯水, but the passage’s manuscript date and earliest surviving physical witness were not established; opening the Ctext text failed. Its citation establishes a received textual cup sense, not a physical-document date.

Later sense pathways, including vessel to classifier and trophy, are not established chronologically from these glosses. Kotobank gives dated Japanese examples for sakazuki, including Man’yōshū (8th century), but those do not date Chinese graph development.

No candidate glyph image met the required identity and reuse-provenance standard. Commons results were modern diagrams or cup-object photographs, not ancient or historical 杯 glyphs. The Commons category page returned a cache-miss access failure.

The local file check found modern Mandarin values 否 fǒu and 桮 bēi (Unihan_Readings.txt rows 45839 and 94483). The task-required official Unicode click-through records were inaccessible, so these exact local values cannot be emitted as externally verified evidence; Unicode’s general documentation does not verify those individual rows.

There is no usable historical pronunciation pair in one reconstruction system for 否 and 桮 in the inspected sources. The local Baxter–Sagart TSV provides 否 *pəʔ but has no 桮 row; it cannot support a same-system comparison. The MOE and CUHK sources give 桮’s 布回切 / Middle Chinese category, but not a matching historical value for 否 there.

Because 否 has multiple modern and historical readings, the Shuowen phonetic statement alone does not select which reading underlies 桮. Modern fǒu–bēi is a descriptive pair, not proof of an ancient sound relationship.

The MOE entry reports its own ancient-character and Han-slip tables as unavailable, while 字源 presents forms labeled Warring States. This research did not inspect a named excavated inscription or establish the physical witness date for those forms.

The received Shuowen account of 桮, the 字源 account of Warring States 不 as a sound element, and the article’s semantic hollowed-tree proposal are distinct scoped analyses. Their exact graphic chronology and the role of 不 in the earliest form remain unresolved.

The Mencius and Zhuangzi passages are received textual citations; this research did not establish the dates of their earliest surviving physical witnesses or a chronological path from vessel to classifier or award sense.

The official Unicode Unihan record URLs for 杯, 不, and 否 could not be opened. Although the supplied local reading extract lists their Mandarin values, those rows are not emitted as externally verified evidence, and no current-reading sound array is proposed.
